title: Wishlist without duplicates
scenario: The same phone appears three times in a wishlist because SKUs arrive as 'ph-12', 'PH-12' and ' PH-12 '.
stack: Spring Boot 4.1.1 · Java 25 · Spring MVC · Java records · HashSet / HashMap · MockMvc
simulation: Five products and two wishlists (7 and 8) are fixed in the code; wishlists live in memory. No login: the wishlist id is in the URL.

tabs.html:
Belongs in this tab

  • The real-life problem as a 3-step story
  • What we are building, and an everyday analogy

  • One question to check yourself
  • What this station is not

Level 1, about 5 minutes. Plain language: no code.

The problem in real life

  1. Ravi wishes for a phone three times

    He taps the heart on the search page, the product page and an old version of the app. Each sends the SKU slightly differently: ph-12, PH-12, ␠PH-12␠.

  2. The wishlist shows the phone three times

    The server's SKU class compared case-insensitively in equals but never defined hashCode, so the HashSet put each copy in a different bucket and never compared them.

  3. The fix

    A record Sku that normalises in its constructor: every spelling becomes PH-12 before it is stored, and records give matching equals and hashCode.

A HashSet asks two questions: "which bucket?" (hashCode) and then "same thing?" (equals). If the answers disagree, duplicates get in.

What are we building?

A wishlist API: add a product by SKU, read the wishlist, remove a product. However a SKU is spelled, it is in the list once, and the list keeps the order products were added.

An everyday analogy

A library shelves books by the first letter of the title. A librarian checks for duplicates only on the shelf where a book belongs. If the shelving rule says "first letter" but the duplicate rule says "same book in any case", then "the hobbit" (shelf t) and "The Hobbit" (shelf T) are never compared, and the library ends up with two. The shelving rule (hashCode) must agree with the duplicate rule (equals).

How it works in 4 steps

  1. The app sends a SKU in any spelling: {"sku": " ph-12 "}.
  2. The Sku record normalises it to PH-12 (or refuses a malformed one with 400).
  3. The catalogue is checked: an unknown product is 422.
  4. The wishlist set adds it: 201 if new, 200 if it was already there. Either way, once.
Check yourself: a key in a HashSet changes its value after being added. Why can the set no longer find it?

The set put it in the bucket for its old hashCode. Looking it up now computes the new hashCode and searches a different bucket. The object is still in the set but cannot be found or removed. That is why keys must be immutable.

What this station is not

  • No login and no database. Two wishlists live in memory.
  • No prices that change. The catalogue is fixed.

Belongs in this tab

  • 1. Business problem

Level 2. What a teammate hands you before you build.

Business problem

Kartwala (the marketplace from station 003) sends price-drop alerts to wishlist owners. Some customers got the same alert three times, because the same phone was in their wishlist three times. The SKU arrives in different spellings from different screens and app versions, and the server's SKU class broke the equals/hashCode contract.

Acceptance criteria

  1. Given an empty wishlist, when ph-12, PH-12 and ␠PH-12␠ are added, then the wishlist holds PH-12 once: 201, then 200, 200.
  2. Given several products, then they are listed in the order first added; adding one again does not move it.
  3. Given a DELETE in any letter case, then 204, and again 204.
  4. Given a malformed SKU, then 400 without echoing it. Given an unknown product, then 422. Given an unknown wishlist, then 404.

Requirements

  • A SKU is 2–30 letters, digits or hyphens, starting with a letter or digit; compared after trimming and upper-casing with Locale.ROOT.
  • Equal SKUs must have equal hash codes; SKUs never change after creation.
  • Each wishlist is a set that keeps insertion order.
  • Errors are RFC 9457 problems that never repeat input.

Learning objectives

  • State the equals/hashCode contract and show what breaks without it.
  • Use records for value equality and immutable keys.
  • Normalise in the constructor, so no unnormalised value exists.
  • Choose HashSet, LinkedHashSet or HashMap for the job.
  • Use the boolean from Set.add instead of a separate contains check.

Status codes

StatusWhen
201The product was added
200The product was already in the list (in any spelling); GET
204Removed (or was not there)
400Missing or malformed SKU
404Unknown wishlist
422Well-formed SKU that is not in the catalogue

Why POST here, after station 008 said POST is not idempotent? Adding to a set is idempotent in effect: the second add changes nothing. The different status (201 then 200) tells the app whether this request added it.

Every edge case points at the test that proves it.

Edge cases

CaseWhat happensProved by
Three spellings of one SKUStored oncetheRealWishlistKeepsOnePhone
Equal SKUsEqual hash codes; not equal to a String or nullequalSkusHaveEqualHashCodes
As keys in HashSet and HashMapOne key per SKUaHashSetAndAHashMapTreatThemAsOneKey
Turkish server localemi-11x still equals MI-11XaTurkishServerLocaleDoesNotChangeTheKey
Empty, one letter, space or underscore inside, 31 characters, nullRefusedmalformedValuesAreRefused

Remove in another case; remove again204, 204removingIs204InAnyLetterCaseAndAgainIs204

Unknown wishlist404anUnknownWishlistIs404

The trap

Plausible but wrong

Overriding equals without hashCode, or using a mutable field as the key.

The "before" OldSku has a careful equals, and a unit test comparing two of them with equals passes. But a HashSet uses hashCode first, and Object.hashCode gives each object its own number, so the three spellings are never compared. The first test shows three phones; the second shows a mutable key getting lost inside a set; the third shows the real API keeping one phone. Removing the upper-casing from Sku was tried while building: 7 tests went red.

package com.kartwala.wishlist;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Import;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

import java.util.HashSet;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.hasSize;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.get;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.post;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.jsonPath;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.status;

/**
 * The first test written for this station: it reproduces the bug before the fix.
 * The same phone arrives as "ph-12" (search page), "PH-12" (product page) and " PH-12 " (an old app).
 */
@Import(EqualsWithoutHashCodeTrapTest.OldWishlistController.class)
class EqualsWithoutHashCodeTrapTest extends ApiTest {

    /** The "before" key: equals ignores case and spaces, but hashCode was never overridden. */
    static final class OldSku {
        final String value;

        OldSku(String value) {
            this.value = value;
        }

        @Override
        public boolean equals(Object o) {
            return o instanceof OldSku other && value.strip().equalsIgnoreCase(other.value.strip());
        }
        // no hashCode(): Object's version gives each object its own number, so HashSet never even calls equals
    }

    /** A key someone can change after it went into the set. */
    static final class MutableSku {
        String value;

        MutableSku(String value) {
            this.value = value;
        }

        @Override
        public boolean equals(Object o) {
            return o instanceof MutableSku other && value.equals(other.value);
        }

        @Override
        public int hashCode() {
            return value.hashCode();
        }
    }

    @RestController
    static class OldWishlistController {
        private final Set<OldSku> items = new HashSet<>();

        @PostMapping("/old/wishlists/7/items")
        synchronized void add(@RequestBody Map<String, String> body) {
            items.add(new OldSku(body.get("sku")));
        }

        @GetMapping("/old/wishlists/7")
        synchronized Object get() {
            return items.stream().map(s -> s.value).toList();
        }
    }

    @Test
    void equalsWithoutHashCodeLetsTheSamePhoneInThreeTimes() throws Exception {
        for (String sku : new String[]{"ph-12", "PH-12", " PH-12 "}) {
            mvc.perform(post("/old/wishlists/7/items").contentType("application/json").content("{\"sku\":\"" + sku + "\"}"))
                    .andExpect(status().isOk());
        }
        mvc.perform(get("/old/wishlists/7")).andExpect(jsonPath("$", hasSize(3))); // the bug from the support ticket
    }

    @Test
    void aKeyChangedAfterInsertionIsLostInsideTheSet() {
        Set<MutableSku> set = new HashSet<>();
        MutableSku phone = new MutableSku("PH-12");
        set.add(phone);
        phone.value = "PH-13";                                    // someone "fixes" the SKU in place
        assertThat(set).hasSize(1);
        assertThat(set.contains(new MutableSku("PH-13"))).isFalse(); // stored in PH-12's bucket, looked up in PH-13's
        assertThat(set.remove(phone)).isFalse();                  // and it cannot even be removed
    }

    @Test
    void theRealWishlistKeepsOnePhone() throws Exception {
        add(7, "ph-12").andExpect(status().isCreated());
        add(7, "PH-12").andExpect(status().isOk());
        add(7, " PH-12 ").andExpect(status().isOk());
        mvc.perform(get("/wishlists/7")).andExpect(jsonPath("$.count").value(1)).andExpect(jsonPath("$.items[0].sku").value("PH-12"));
    }
}

Code walkthrough

src/main/java/com/kartwala/wishlist/WishlistController.java

Does
Three endpoints. Turns raw text into a Sku (or 400), checks the catalogue (422), adds, and answers 201 or 200.
Why
All HTTP decisions in one place.
Without it
No API.
  • wishlists.add returns whether the set changed, which picks the status: no separate contains check that could race.
package com.kartwala.wishlist;

import jakarta.validation.Valid;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotNull;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity;
import org.springframework.web.ErrorResponseException;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.DeleteMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

import java.util.List;

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/wishlists/{id}")
class WishlistController {

    record AddItem(@NotNull String sku) {
    }

    record Item(String sku, String name, int pricePaise) {
    }

    record WishlistView(long wishlistId, int count, List<Item> items) {
    }

    private final Wishlists wishlists;
    private final Catalog catalog;

    WishlistController(Wishlists wishlists, Catalog catalog) {
        this.wishlists = wishlists;
        this.catalog = catalog;
    }

    @GetMapping
    WishlistView get(@PathVariable long id) {
        return view(id);
    }

    /** 201 if the product was added, 200 if it was already there. Either way it is in the list exactly once. */
    @PostMapping("/items")
    ResponseEntity<WishlistView> add(@PathVariable long id, @Valid @RequestBody AddItem request) {
        requireWishlist(id);
        Sku sku = sku(request.sku());
        if (catalog.find(sku).isEmpty()) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, "Unknown product", "No product has this SKU.");
        }
        boolean added = wishlists.add(id, sku);
        return ResponseEntity.status(added ? HttpStatus.CREATED : HttpStatus.OK).body(view(id));
    }

    /** 204 whether or not it was in the list: removing twice is safe (station 008). */
    @DeleteMapping("/items/{sku}")
    ResponseEntity<Void> remove(@PathVariable long id, @PathVariable String sku) {
        requireWishlist(id);
        wishlists.remove(id, sku(sku));
        return ResponseEntity.noContent().build();
    }

    private WishlistView view(long id) {
        List<Item> items = wishlists.items(id).orElseThrow(WishlistController::notFound).stream()
                .map(sku -> catalog.find(sku).orElseThrow())
                .map(p -> new Item(p.sku().value(), p.name(), p.pricePaise()))
                .toList();
        return new WishlistView(id, items.size(), items);
    }

    private static Sku sku(String raw) {
        try {
            return new Sku(raw);
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "Invalid SKU", e.getMessage()); // our own fixed message, not the input
        }
    }

    private void requireWishlist(long id) {
        if (!wishlists.exists(id)) {
            throw notFound();
        }
    }

    private static ErrorResponseException notFound() {
        return problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Wishlist not found", "No wishlist has this id.");
    }

    private static ErrorResponseException problem(HttpStatus status, String title, String detail) {
        ProblemDetail body = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(status, detail);
        body.setTitle(title);
        return new ErrorResponseException(status, body, null);
    }
}

src/main/java/com/kartwala/wishlist/Sku.java

Does
The key: one normalised, validated, immutable value.
Why
A record gives equals and hashCode from the same field, so they always agree; normalising in the constructor means no unnormalised SKU can exist.
Without it
Every caller would have to remember to trim and upper-case, and one would forget.
package com.kartwala.wishlist;

import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.regex.Pattern;

/**
 * A stock-keeping unit, the product's code. A record: equals and hashCode come from its one field, so two Skus
 * with the same value are equal and land in the same HashSet bucket. Immutable: once a Sku is a key in a set or
 * map, it can never change underneath it.
 *
 * The constructor normalises before anything can compare it: "ph-12", "PH-12" and " PH-12 " all become "PH-12".
 * Normalise first, compare second; the other order is how the wishlist got three phones.
 */
public record Sku(String value) {

    private static final Pattern SHAPE = Pattern.compile("[A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9-]{1,29}");

    public Sku {
        if (value == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("A SKU is required.");
        }
        value = value.strip().toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT); // Locale.ROOT: on a Turkish server "mi-11" must not become "Mİ-11"
        if (!SHAPE.matcher(value).matches()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("A SKU is 2-30 letters, digits or hyphens, like PH-12.");
        }
    }

    @Override
    public String toString() {
        return value;
    }
}

src/main/java/com/kartwala/wishlist/Wishlists.java

Does
Holds a LinkedHashSet<Sku> per wishlist.
Why
A set refuses duplicates by itself; "linked" keeps the order they were added.
Without it
A list, where duplicates need manual checks.
package com.kartwala.wishlist;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

import java.util.LinkedHashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.Set;

/**
 * Each wishlist is a LinkedHashSet of Skus: a set, so a Sku can be in it once; linked, so it keeps the order
 * items were added. In memory; synchronized so two requests do not interleave.
 */
@Component
class Wishlists {

    private final Map<Long, Set<Sku>> lists = Map.of(7L, new LinkedHashSet<>(), 8L, new LinkedHashSet<>());

    boolean exists(long id) {
        return lists.containsKey(id);
    }

    /** True if the Sku was added, false if it was already there. Set.add tells us: no separate contains() check. */
    synchronized boolean add(long id, Sku sku) {
        return lists.get(id).add(sku);
    }

    synchronized void remove(long id, Sku sku) {
        lists.get(id).remove(sku);
    }

    synchronized Optional<List<Sku>> items(long id) {
        return Optional.ofNullable(lists.get(id)).map(List::copyOf);
    }

    /** For tests only. */
    synchronized void clear() {
        lists.values().forEach(Set::clear);
    }
}

src/main/java/com/kartwala/wishlist/Catalog.java

Does
The products, in a Map<Sku, Product>.
Why
Shows a record used as a map key: lookups by an equal Sku find the product.
Without it
No names or prices in the wishlist.
package com.kartwala.wishlist;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Optional;

/** The products that can be wished for. A HashMap keyed by Sku: lookups work because Sku has value equality. */
@Component
class Catalog {

    record Product(Sku sku, String name, int pricePaise) {
    }

    private final Map<Sku, Product> products = Map.of(
            new Sku("PH-12"), new Product(new Sku("PH-12"), "Samsung Galaxy M35 5G", 1_699_900),
            new Sku("TV-55"), new Product(new Sku("TV-55"), "Samsung 55-inch Crystal TV", 4_299_000),
            new Sku("EB-141"), new Product(new Sku("EB-141"), "boAt Airdopes 141", 129_900),
            new Sku("MI-11X"), new Product(new Sku("MI-11X"), "Redmi Note 13", 1_799_900),
            new Sku("CK-5L"), new Product(new Sku("CK-5L"), "Prestige Pressure Cooker 5L", 249_900));

    Optional<Product> find(Sku sku) {
        return Optional.ofNullable(products.get(sku));
    }
}

import org.springframework.http.HttpHeaders;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatusCode;
import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity;
import org.springframework.web.bind.MethodArgumentNotValidException;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestControllerAdvice;
import org.springframework.web.context.request.WebRequest;
import org.springframework.web.servlet.mvc.method.annotation.ResponseEntityExceptionHandler;

import java.util.Map;
import java.util.TreeMap;

/**
 * Spring already turns an invalid @Valid body into an RFC 9457 problem (the base class). We add an "errors" map,
 * field -> message, so the form can show each message next to its input. Station 006 covers error handling in depth.
 */
@RestControllerAdvice
class ApiErrors extends ResponseEntityExceptionHandler {

    @Override
    protected ResponseEntity<Object> handleMethodArgumentNotValid(
            MethodArgumentNotValidException ex, HttpHeaders headers, HttpStatusCode status, WebRequest request) {
        Map<String, String> errors = new TreeMap<>();
        ex.getBindingResult().getFieldErrors().forEach(e -> errors.putIfAbsent(e.getField(), e.getDefaultMessage()));
        ex.getBody().setDetail("The request has invalid fields.");
        ex.getBody().setProperty("errors", errors);
        return handleExceptionInternal(ex, null, headers, status, request);
    }
}

Written first: three phones from a broken key; a lost mutable key; one phone with the record.

package com.kartwala.wishlist;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Import;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

import java.util.HashSet;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.hamcrest.Matchers.hasSize;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.get;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.request.MockMvcRequestBuilders.post;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.jsonPath;
import static org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.status;

/**
 * The first test written for this station: it reproduces the bug before the fix.
 * The same phone arrives as "ph-12" (search page), "PH-12" (product page) and " PH-12 " (an old app).
 */
@Import(EqualsWithoutHashCodeTrapTest.OldWishlistController.class)
class EqualsWithoutHashCodeTrapTest extends ApiTest {

    /** The "before" key: equals ignores case and spaces, but hashCode was never overridden. */
    static final class OldSku {
        final String value;

        OldSku(String value) {
            this.value = value;
        }

        @Override
        public boolean equals(Object o) {
            return o instanceof OldSku other && value.strip().equalsIgnoreCase(other.value.strip());
        }
        // no hashCode(): Object's version gives each object its own number, so HashSet never even calls equals
    }

    /** A key someone can change after it went into the set. */
    static final class MutableSku {
        String value;

        MutableSku(String value) {
            this.value = value;
        }

        @Override
        public boolean equals(Object o) {
            return o instanceof MutableSku other && value.equals(other.value);
        }

        @Override
        public int hashCode() {
            return value.hashCode();
        }
    }

    @RestController
    static class OldWishlistController {
        private final Set<OldSku> items = new HashSet<>();

        @PostMapping("/old/wishlists/7/items")
        synchronized void add(@RequestBody Map<String, String> body) {
            items.add(new OldSku(body.get("sku")));
        }

        @GetMapping("/old/wishlists/7")
        synchronized Object get() {
            return items.stream().map(s -> s.value).toList();
        }
    }

    @Test
    void equalsWithoutHashCodeLetsTheSamePhoneInThreeTimes() throws Exception {
        for (String sku : new String[]{"ph-12", "PH-12", " PH-12 "}) {
            mvc.perform(post("/old/wishlists/7/items").contentType("application/json").content("{\"sku\":\"" + sku + "\"}"))
                    .andExpect(status().isOk());
        }
        mvc.perform(get("/old/wishlists/7")).andExpect(jsonPath("$", hasSize(3))); // the bug from the support ticket
    }

    @Test
    void aKeyChangedAfterInsertionIsLostInsideTheSet() {
        Set<MutableSku> set = new HashSet<>();
        MutableSku phone = new MutableSku("PH-12");
        set.add(phone);
        phone.value = "PH-13";                                    // someone "fixes" the SKU in place
        assertThat(set).hasSize(1);
        assertThat(set.contains(new MutableSku("PH-13"))).isFalse(); // stored in PH-12's bucket, looked up in PH-13's
        assertThat(set.remove(phone)).isFalse();                  // and it cannot even be removed
    }

    @Test
    void theRealWishlistKeepsOnePhone() throws Exception {
        add(7, "ph-12").andExpect(status().isCreated());
        add(7, "PH-12").andExpect(status().isOk());
        add(7, " PH-12 ").andExpect(status().isOk());
        mvc.perform(get("/wishlists/7")).andExpect(jsonPath("$.count").value(1)).andExpect(jsonPath("$.items[0].sku").value("PH-12"));
    }
}

package com.kartwala.wishlist;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.AfterEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.HashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Set;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;

/** The key on its own: the equals/hashCode contract, normalising, and use in HashSet and HashMap. */
class SkuTest {

    private final Locale original = Locale.getDefault();

    @AfterEach
    void restoreLocale() {
        Locale.setDefault(original);
    }

    @Test
    void equalSkusHaveEqualHashCodes() {
        List<Sku> same = List.of(new Sku("ph-12"), new Sku("PH-12"), new Sku(" PH-12 "), new Sku("Ph-12\t"));
        for (Sku a : same) {
            for (Sku b : same) {
                assertThat(a).isEqualTo(b);
                assertThat(a.hashCode()).isEqualTo(b.hashCode()); // the half of the contract the trap forgot
            }
        }
        assertThat(new Sku("PH-12")).isNotEqualTo(new Sku("PH-13")).isNotEqualTo(null).isNotEqualTo("PH-12");
    }

    @Test
    void aHashSetAndAHashMapTreatThemAsOneKey() {
        Set<Sku> set = new HashSet<>(List.of(new Sku("ph-12"), new Sku("PH-12"), new Sku(" PH-12 ")));
        assertThat(set).containsExactly(new Sku("PH-12"));
        Map<Sku, Integer> wishes = new HashMap<>();
        for (String raw : List.of("ph-12", "PH-12", "tv-55")) {
            wishes.merge(new Sku(raw), 1, Integer::sum);
        }
        assertThat(wishes).containsEntry(new Sku("PH-12"), 2).containsEntry(new Sku("TV-55"), 1);
    }

    @Test
    void aTurkishServerLocaleDoesNotChangeTheKey() {
        Locale.setDefault(Locale.forLanguageTag("tr-TR")); // "mi-11x".toUpperCase() would be "Mİ-11X"
        assertThat(new Sku("mi-11x")).isEqualTo(new Sku("MI-11X"));
    }

    @Test
    void malformedValuesAreRefused() {
        for (String bad : new String[]{"", "   ", "P", "-PH", "PH 12", "PH_12", "A".repeat(31)}) {
            assertThatThrownBy(() -> new Sku(bad)).as(bad).isInstanceOf(IllegalArgumentException.class);
        }
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> new Sku(null)).isInstanceOf(IllegalArgumentException.class);
    }
}

package com.kartwala.wishlist;

import jakarta.validation.Valid;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotNull;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.http.ProblemDetail;
import org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity;
import org.springframework.web.ErrorResponseException;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.DeleteMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

import java.util.List;

@RestController
@RequestMapping("/wishlists/{id}")
class WishlistController {

    record AddItem(@NotNull String sku) {
    }

    record Merge(@NotNull List<String> skus) {
    }

    record Item(String sku, String name, int pricePaise) {
    }

    record WishlistView(long wishlistId, int count, List<Item> items) {
    }

    private final Wishlists wishlists;
    private final Catalog catalog;

    WishlistController(Wishlists wishlists, Catalog catalog) {
        this.wishlists = wishlists;
        this.catalog = catalog;
    }

    @GetMapping
    WishlistView get(@PathVariable long id) {
        return view(id);
    }

    /** 201 if the product was added, 200 if it was already there. Either way it is in the list exactly once. */
    @PostMapping("/items")
    ResponseEntity<WishlistView> add(@PathVariable long id, @Valid @RequestBody AddItem request) {
        requireWishlist(id);
        Sku sku = sku(request.sku());
        if (catalog.find(sku).isEmpty()) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, "Unknown product", "No product has this SKU.");
        }
        boolean added = wishlists.add(id, sku);
        return ResponseEntity.status(added ? HttpStatus.CREATED : HttpStatus.OK).body(view(id));
    }

    /** Challenge 1: check every SKU first, then add them all. One bad SKU and nothing is merged. */
    @PostMapping("/merge")
    WishlistView merge(@PathVariable long id, @Valid @RequestBody Merge request) {
        requireWishlist(id);
        List<Sku> skus = request.skus().stream().map(WishlistController::sku).toList();
        if (skus.stream().anyMatch(s -> catalog.find(s).isEmpty())) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, "Unknown product", "At least one SKU is not in the catalogue.");
        }
        wishlists.addAll(id, skus);
        return view(id);
    }

    /** 204 whether or not it was in the list: removing twice is safe (station 008). */
    @DeleteMapping("/items/{sku}")
    ResponseEntity<Void> remove(@PathVariable long id, @PathVariable String sku) {
        requireWishlist(id);
        wishlists.remove(id, sku(sku));
        return ResponseEntity.noContent().build();
    }

    private WishlistView view(long id) {
        List<Item> items = wishlists.items(id).orElseThrow(WishlistController::notFound).stream()
                .map(sku -> catalog.find(sku).orElseThrow())
                .map(p -> new Item(p.sku().value(), p.name(), p.pricePaise()))
                .toList();
        return new WishlistView(id, items.size(), items);
    }

    private static Sku sku(String raw) {
        try {
            return new Sku(raw);
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
            throw problem(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "Invalid SKU", e.getMessage()); // our own fixed message, not the input
        }
    }

    private void requireWishlist(long id) {
        if (!wishlists.exists(id)) {
            throw notFound();
        }
    }

    private static ErrorResponseException notFound() {
        return problem(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Wishlist not found", "No wishlist has this id.");
    }

    private static ErrorResponseException problem(HttpStatus status, String title, String detail) {
        ProblemDetail body = ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(status, detail);
        body.setTitle(title);
        return new ErrorResponseException(status, body, null);
    }
}

package com.kartwala.wishlist;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.LinkedHashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.Set;

/**
 * Each wishlist is a LinkedHashSet of Skus: a set, so a Sku can be in it once; linked, so it keeps the order
 * items were added. In memory; synchronized so two requests do not interleave.
 */
@Component
class Wishlists {

    private final Map<Long, Set<Sku>> lists = Map.of(7L, new LinkedHashSet<>(), 8L, new LinkedHashSet<>());

    boolean exists(long id) {
        return lists.containsKey(id);
    }

    /** True if the Sku was added, false if it was already there. Set.add tells us: no separate contains() check. */
    synchronized boolean add(long id, Sku sku) {
        return lists.get(id).add(sku);
    }

    /** Challenge 1: the whole list in one step, under one lock. Set.addAll skips what is already there. */
    synchronized void addAll(long id, List<Sku> skus) {
        lists.get(id).addAll(skus);
    }

    /** Challenge 2: Sku -> number of wishlists that hold it. A HashMap keyed by a record works because of value equality. */
    synchronized Map<Sku, Integer> counts() {
        Map<Sku, Integer> counts = new HashMap<>();
        lists.values().forEach(list -> list.forEach(sku -> counts.merge(sku, 1, Integer::sum)));
        return counts;
    }

    synchronized void remove(long id, Sku sku) {
        lists.get(id).remove(sku);
    }

    synchronized Optional<List<Sku>> items(long id) {
        return Optional.ofNullable(lists.get(id)).map(List::copyOf);
    }

    /** For tests only. */
    synchronized void clear() {
        lists.values().forEach(Set::clear);
    }
}

/** Challenge 2. Counting happens in a HashMap<Sku, Integer>; ranking sorts its entries. */
@RestController
class MostWishedController {

    record Wished(String sku, int wishlists) {
    }

    private final Wishlists wishlists;

    MostWishedController(Wishlists wishlists) {
        this.wishlists = wishlists;
    }

    @GetMapping("/products/most-wished")
    List<Wished> mostWished(@RequestParam(defaultValue = "10") @Min(1) @Max(50) int limit) {
        return wishlists.counts().entrySet().stream()
                .sorted(Map.Entry.<Sku, Integer>comparingByValue().reversed()
                        .thenComparing(e -> e.getKey().value()))
                .limit(limit)
                .map(e -> new Wished(e.getKey().value(), e.getValue()))
                .toList();
    }
}

package com.kartwala.wishlist;

import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.LinkedHashSet;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.Set;

/**
 * Each wishlist is a LinkedHashSet of Skus: a set, so a Sku can be in it once; linked, so it keeps the order
 * items were added. In memory; synchronized so two requests do not interleave.
 */
@Component
class Wishlists {

    private final Map<Long, Set<Sku>> lists = Map.of(7L, new LinkedHashSet<>(), 8L, new LinkedHashSet<>());

    boolean exists(long id) {
        return lists.containsKey(id);
    }

    /** True if the Sku was added, false if it was already there. Set.add tells us: no separate contains() check. */
    synchronized boolean add(long id, Sku sku) {
        return lists.get(id).add(sku);
    }

    /** Challenge 1: the whole list in one step, under one lock. Set.addAll skips what is already there. */
    synchronized void addAll(long id, List<Sku> skus) {
        lists.get(id).addAll(skus);
    }

    /** Challenge 2: Sku -> number of wishlists that hold it. A HashMap keyed by a record works because of value equality. */
    synchronized Map<Sku, Integer> counts() {
        Map<Sku, Integer> counts = new HashMap<>();
        lists.values().forEach(list -> list.forEach(sku -> counts.merge(sku, 1, Integer::sum)));
        return counts;
    }

    synchronized void remove(long id, Sku sku) {
        lists.get(id).remove(sku);
    }

    synchronized Optional<List<Sku>> items(long id) {
        return Optional.ofNullable(lists.get(id)).map(List::copyOf);
    }

    /** For tests only. */
    synchronized void clear() {
        lists.values().forEach(Set::clear);
    }
}

Short at Foundations: the choices that matter here.

Implementation approach

  1. Write the trap test: equals without hashCode lets three phones in.
  2. Make Sku a record that normalises and validates in its constructor.
  3. Store each wishlist as a LinkedHashSet<Sku>; use add's boolean for the status.
  4. Test the contract pair by pair, and in real sets and maps.

Design alternatives and trade-offs

ApproachWhat it costsVerdict
Record that normalises in its constructorNothing; the canonical value is all that exists.Chosen
Class with case-insensitive equals and no hashCodeDuplicates in every hash collection (the trap).Wrong
Class with matching case-insensitive equals and hashCodeWorks, but every method must remember the rule, and the response shows whichever spelling came first.Possible
TreeSet with String.CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDERUses a comparator instead of equals; loses insertion order; ignores spaces only if you trim first.Possible
Lombok @EqualsAndHashCodeGenerated and consistent, but a dependency for what records already do.Not needed

Database design

None in this station. With a database, the same rule is a primary key (wishlist_id, sku) plus a check that sku = upper(trim(sku)), so a script cannot insert a second spelling.

A Foundations station: the considerations to know, no runbook.

Correctness
Every place that compares SKUs gets the same answer, because there is one normalised form. Price-drop alerts go out once per product.
Performance
Hash lookups take constant time on average. A broken hashCode that returns the same number for everything is "correct" but turns every set into a slow list.
Security
The wishlist id in the URL is a demo shortcut; real apps take it from the login. A malformed SKU is refused with a fixed message.
Maintainability
Changing the SKU rule (say, allowing dots) is one pattern in one record.

Interview takeaways

What is the equals/hashCode contract?

If two objects are equal by equals, they must have the same hashCode. (Equal hash codes do not have to mean equal objects.) Hash collections rely on it: they find the bucket with hashCode, then compare with equals.

What happens if you override equals but not hashCode?

Equal objects get different hash codes (Object's version), land in different buckets, and are never compared. HashSet keeps duplicates; HashMap lookups by an equal key return null.

Why must map keys be immutable?

The bucket is chosen when the key is inserted. If the key's fields change, its hashCode changes, and lookups search the wrong bucket: the entry is still there but cannot be found or removed.

What do records give you?

A constructor, accessors, and equals, hashCode and toString based on all components. Fields are final, so records make good keys, as long as their components are immutable too.

Why normalise in the constructor rather than in equals?

Then only canonical values exist: equals, hashCode, toString, JSON output and database storage all see the same form, with no rule repeated.
